phases.message: I'm Mom's representative payee and Social Security wants my yearly report. Start in my folder: my appointment letter, my notes, last year's report and the receipts I want paid back.
Oakview Care. Read Mom's agreement and her invoices. Pay what she owes that's due, and dispute anything she shouldn't be charged.

Ledgerline, Mom's payee accounts. Go through the year's statements, her savings and this month's activity. Pay me back for what I bought her, and fix anything that came out of her account that shouldn't have.
Benefitline. Read the rules, her payments and the report they've asked for, then file it with the right figures. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

documents.title: Representative payee appointment letter
documents.text: Notice, 18 October 2024. Carla Holloway, the daughter of Agnes Holloway, is selected as her representative payee for Social Security retirement benefits from November 2024. Agnes lives at Oakview Care, 900 Oak Ridge Road, in assisted living. The payee must use the benefits for Agnes's needs, keep them in an account titled to show Agnes owns them, keep records, and account for them every year when asked. Agnes receives no Supplemental Security Income.

documents.title: My notes: what Mom's money pays for
documents.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026 as I add the last line. Mom's Social Security is her only income in the payee account. Oakview's board and care is her rent and meals. Pharmacy, salon, clothes, glasses and hearing aid batteries are hers. I keep my own bills on my own account; Brightcell is MY phone (account 77-3190). I'm her daughter, not her spouse, and she doesn't live with me.

agreement.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Residency agreement between Oakview Care and Agnes Holloway (Carla Holloway, representative payee, signs for payment). Sections: rates, care-levels, billing.

Assisted living, private studio, care level 2: $1,550 a month for board and care: the room, three meals a day, housekeeping and the services of care level 2. Guest meals for visitors: $14 each, billed to the visitor, or to the resident's account if the visitor asks.

Care level 1: room, meals, housekeeping. Care level 2 (Agnes, since March 2025): level 1 plus help with bathing and dressing, and medication management (staff keep, set up and give her medicines). Medication management is charged at $45 a month only to residents on care level 1 who ask for it.

Board and care is billed on the 1st and due on the 10th of the month; after the 10th a late fee of $50 is added. Other charges are billed as they arise and due in 30 days. A disputed invoice is held while the business office answers.

invoices.for: Guest meals, 27 September 2026: 3 at $14 (Carla Holloway and her two children), billed to Agnes's account

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Representative payee rules, under 20 CFR 404.2035 (duties), 404.2040 and 404.2045 (use of benefits), 404.2065 (accounting) and SSA's payee guidance. Topics: duties, use, reimbursement, exemptions, report.

A payee must use the benefits only for the beneficiary's use and benefit; keep them separate from the payee's own money, in an account that shows the beneficiary owns them; treat interest as the beneficiary's; tell SSA of changes that affect the benefits or the payee's duties; and account for the benefits in writing when SSA asks, keeping records to support it (20 CFR 404.2035). Using any of the benefits for anyone else is misuse; money that left the beneficiary's account for someone else must be paid back to it.

Benefits go first to current maintenance: food, shelter, clothing, medical care and personal comfort items (20 CFR 404.2040(a)). For a beneficiary in a care facility, that includes the facility's customary charges and her personal needs. What is left is saved for the beneficiary, in an account titled to show the payee holds it for her (404.2045).

A payee may pay herself back from the beneficiary's benefits for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses she actually paid for the beneficiary, with receipts, and only the amount paid (SSA payee guidance). Never for the payee's own expenses. A payee who is a person, not an approved organization, may never charge a fee for her services or time (20 CFR 404.2040a).

Since the Strengthening Protections for Social Security Beneficiaries Act of 2018, four kinds of payee do not file the annual report (20 CFR 404.2065(b)): a natural or adoptive parent of a minor child, or a legal guardian of one, who primarily lives in the same household; a natural or adoptive parent of a disabled adult who primarily lives in the same household; and the beneficiary's spouse. Every other payee files every year when asked.

Form SSA-623 covers the 12 months ending with the month the report was asked for. Line 1: benefits received for her in the period. Line 2: spent on food and housing. Line 3: spent on everything else (clothing, medical, personal items, recreation). Line 4: saved: the amount in savings for her at the end of the period, including savings from earlier periods and interest. Lines 2 to 4 should account for the total: benefits received plus the savings on the last report. Spending after the period belongs to next year's report.
